then.text: Mind and season that girdle before the Antarctic. A wee bit of fat, a good heat. Oatcakes on the ice! I'm jealous, and I don't even like the cold.

else.text: A girdle for the Discovery? For oatcakes at the bottom of the world? Oh, that's the best order I've had all year.
In 1599 King James the Sixth gave the hammermen of Culross the sole right to make girdles in Scotland. Every girdle in every kitchen came from this wee town.
Here. Hammered round, flat as the Forth on a good day. Take it to the Bosun with my compliments.
A girdle is a flat iron plate you bake on over the fire: oatcakes, scones, drop scones, pancakes. Up here we say girdle. Down south they say griddle. They're wrong, nicely.
Culross had the monopoly on them from 1599. A royal monopoly. On a frying pan. It was a big deal at the time.
